efet_body:
Cyclone Akvan forecast track changes, heavy rain alert withdrawn for Telangana’s four districts
Published
- November 18, 2026 05:02 pm IST - HYDERABAD
The Hindu Bureau

Remove
According to India Meteorological Department’s latest observed and forecast track of cyclonic storm Akvan released on Wednesday, it may not make its way into Telangana
| Photo Credit: INDIA METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT
The heavy to very heavy rainfall forecast for a few districts of
Telangana was withdrawn as the cyclonic storm Akvan
may not make its way to the State after it weakens into depression.
Changes in forecast track
The cyclonic storm is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), as per the latest information from India Meteorological Department (IMD). While earlier observed and forecast track of the cyclone predicted it may enter Telangana, the latest track shows it may head to Odisha instead.
Heavy rain forecast for Telangana withdrawn
While the IMD-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall and thunderstorms accompanied by lightning as very likely to occur at isolated places in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet and Mahabubabad on Friday, this was withdrawn.
Thunderstorm forecast for Telangana
According to its latest weather bulletin issued in the afternoon on Wednesday, only thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are predicted as very likely at isolated places in the four districts and in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu and Nalgonda on Friday. The same weather conditions may be witnessed in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam and Suryapet on Thursday.

news_title: FDA seizes suspected substandard edible oil worth ₹50.27 lakh in Pune district

FDA seizes suspected substandard edible oil worth ₹50.27 lakh in Pune district
During the inspection, authorities seized the entire stock of 20,085 litres of edible oil, valued at ₹50.27 lakh, suspecting violations relating to substandard quality and misbranding under the Food Safety and Standards Act
Updated
- November 18, 2026 04:39 pm IST - Pune
PTI
READ LATER
SEE ALL
Remove
The action was carried out on November 17 at the company’s facility in Ambi village in Maval taluka. File.
| Photo Credit: Reuters
The
Maharashtra
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has seized 20,085 litres of edible oil from an Avenue Supermarts Limited facility in Pune district over suspicion that the stock was substandard and misbranded, and collected samples of edible oil sold under several popular brands, officials said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
The action was carried out on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) at the company's facility in Ambi village in Maval taluka, the regulator said in a release. Avenue Supermarts operates the popular D-Mart retail chain.
FDA suspends 105 licences, cancels 7 across Maharashtra after pre-Deepavali checks
During the inspection, authorities seized the entire stock of 20,085 litres of edible oil, valued at ₹50.27 lakh, suspecting violations relating to substandard quality and misbranding under the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The FDA collected nine samples, including refined sunflower oil sold under the Aadhar brand, physically refined rice bran oil sold under the Fortune brand, Kachi Ghani mustard oil sold under the Patanjali brand, and cold-pressed mustard and groundnut oils sold under the Saffola brand, the release said.
The samples have been sent to a laboratory for analysis, and further legal action will be taken after the reports are received, said Shrikant Karkale, joint commissioner, FDA (food).

news_title: WBHRC directs DG Prisons to submit a report on the poor living conditions at Midnapore Correctional Home
efet_title: WBHRC directs DG Prisons to submit a report on the poor living conditions at Midnapore Correctional Home
efet_body:
WBHRC directs DG Prisons to submit a report on the poor living conditions at Midnapore Correctional Home
The development came in the wake of a formal complaint by general secretary of the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APR), Altaf Ahmed, with the State’s human rights commission recently
Updated
- November 18, 2026 04:09 pm IST - KOLKATA
Senjuti Sengupta
READ LATER
SEE ALL
Remove
The West Bengal Human Rights Commission (WBHRC) has sought a detailed report from the Director General (DG) of Correctional Services on the poor living conditions and lack of infrastructure for inmates at Midnapore Central Correctional Home.
The development came in the wake of a formal complaint by general secretary of the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR), Altaf Ahmed, with the State’s Human Rights Commission recently. Over the last few months, a delegation from the organisation repeatedly visited the Midnapore jail and spoke with a section of inmates, families visiting prisoners and those who had been released or granted bail.
Based on their visits, APDR members also submitted a memorandum to the jail superintendent. However, as the situation failed to improve, APDR approached the State Human Rights Commission with a complaint last August and also submitted a memorandum to the Inspector General (Prisons).
“The West Bengal Human Rights Commission has sought a report from the Director General of Prisons (DG Prisons) regarding the pathetic state of the Midnapore Central Correctional Home, specifically concerning the quality and quantity of food and the mismanagement of medical treatment,” said APDR vice president said in a statement.
Apart from the quantity and quality of food and medical facilities, a major issue at this jail during the monsoon is rainwater leaking heavily through the roofs of certain wards, causing immense suffering to the inmates. Repeatedly bringing this to the attention of authorities yielded no results, it added. After receiving the complaint from APDR, the WBHRC directed the DG to take immediate cognisance of the matter and submit the report within seven weeks.
Earlier this year, an outbreak of Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) was reported at Jalpaiguri Central Correctional Home, with over 90 infections and seven of infected inmates losing their lives. As per the 2023 Prison Statistics of India, a report published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, district prisons in West Bengal have reported an occupancy rate of 158%. The prisons in the State are also burdened by a high number of inmates who are foreign nationals, particularly those from Bangladesh.

View Market Dashboard Old Monk sales ban: Rum maker withdraws court plea, agrees to revise labels after FSSAI objections Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, which makes Old Monk, has withdrawn its Bombay High Court petition challenging an FSSAI order restricting the sale and distribution of certain products. The company told the court it would revise the labels and submit them to the regulator for approval. Anjali Thakur Published 7 Nov 2026, 06:49 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Old Monk sales ban: Rum maker withdraws court plea, agrees to revise labels after FSSAI objections ( Instagram/oldmonk_indiaa ) AI Quick Read Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries Pvt Ltd, the maker of the Old Monk rum brand, has withdrawn its petition before the Bombay High Court challenging a sales restriction imposed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over the labelling and product descriptions of certain variants. FSSAI had objected to the use of the term "rum" on products containing added flavouring agents, directing that they be labelled and marketed as "rum-flavoured spirit" instead. The regulator had also raised concerns over descriptions such as "7 Years Old Blended" and "Very Old Vatted". The authority had barred the sale and distribution of several Old Monk products manufactured at the company's Khopoli facility. Also Read | Tanvi Patri’s father recalls Youth Olympics final heartbreak: ‘Papa, I lost…’ Old Monk maker agrees to revise product labels During a hearing on Thursday, a bench led by Chief Justice Maheshchandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna was informed by the company that it would revise the product labels and submit the updated versions to FSSAI for approval. The company's decision to withdraw its petition follows the court's refusal to grant interim relief against the regulator's order. Why did FSSAI restrict the sale of certain Old Monk products? The dispute centres on the classification and labelling of certain Old Monk variants. FSSAI's objection was that products containing added flavouring agents should be described as "rum-flavoured spirit" rather than "rum". The regulator also questioned the use of age-related and product descriptions such as "7 Years Old Blended" and "Very Old Vatted". Also Read | Diwali Muhurat trading: Why do NSE, BSE open for live trading session on Diwali? The sales and distribution restriction applied to several products manufactured at the company's Khopoli facility. Old Monk maker had cited over ₹ 350 crore loss in excise revenue The brewer had earlier argued that the sales restriction had resulted in a loss of more than ₹ 350 crore in excise revenue for the Maharashtra government. Also Read | Liam Lawson faces uncertain F1 future as Racing Bulls delay 2027 decision However, after the Bombay High Court declined to grant interim relief against the FSSAI order, the company chose not to pursue the case on merits and withdrew its petition. The court subsequently disposed of the matter. news_title: US court directs Pannun case documents to be sent to Delhi courts
efet_title: US court directs Pannun case documents to be sent to Delhi courts
efet_body:
US court directs Pannun case documents to be sent to Delhi courts
India has rejected Pannun’s lawsuit, calling it “fabricated and malicious”.
Published on: Nov 18, 2026, 08:24:10 IST
By
HT Correspondent
Prefer HT
on Google
Share via
Copy link
A US court has directed that documents linked to a case filed by Khalistani separatist
Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
be sent to three district courts in Delhi for delivery to National Security Adviser (NSA)
Ajit Doval
and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief Samant Goel.
The US State Department transmitted a civil lawsuit filed by Pannun against the Indian government to the Indian embassy in Washington through diplomatic channels. (File)
India has rejected Pannun’s lawsuit, calling it “fabricated and malicious”. The latest court order does not establish any liability on the part of the two officials.
In an order issued on Tuesday, the US District Court for the Southern District of New York directed its clerk to send the summons and accompanying judicial documents to the Patiala House District Court for Doval and the Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts for Goel.
“The clerk of this court is directed to transmit the accompanying service materials, by international mail or courier, to the…Indian courts having jurisdiction where Defendants reside,” the order said.
Last week, the US State Department transmitted a civil lawsuit filed by Pannun against the Indian government to the Indian embassy in Washington through diplomatic channels. Separately, the New York court cleared the way for Pannun to serve summons on Doval and Goel through Indian courts.
The two developments marked separate steps in the process of formally notifying the defendants in the civil suit, which alleges that Indian officials conspired to assassinate Pannun at his New York home in 2023. Neither, however, amounts to a judicial finding on the allegations.
India has long raised with the US the activities of Pannun and other Khalistani separatists based in North America, including threats issued by them against Indian diplomats and missions.
The Indian side has also apprised the US of what it describes as the frivolous nature of legal cases filed by the separatists.
On November 11, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal dismissed Pannun’s case when asked about it at a regular media briefing and stressed that all official communications related to the issue would have to be routed through India’s law ministry.

FSSAI cracks down on unsafe food, suspends licence, orders recall
In a major regulatory crackdown to safeguard consumer health, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has taken stern action against multiple food manufacturers, suspending the operational licence of a confectionery firm over grave hygiene lapses and ordering an immediate market recall of packaged cumin powder found to be "unsafe."

The regulator also flagged a dairy whitener sample as substandard, intensifying enforcement to protect consumer health.
In a major regulatory crackdown to safeguard consumer health, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has taken stern action against multiple food manufacturers, suspending the operational licence of a confectionery firm over grave
hygiene lapses
and ordering an immediate market recall of packaged cumin powder found to be "unsafe."
According to regulatory directives, the manufacturing licence of a bakery and confectionery manufacturing unit has been suspended with immediate effect after food safety authorities discovered critical non-compliance and severe deficiencies in sanitation and hygienic practices during inspections.
Under the enforcement order, the manufacturing unit has been barred from producing or distributing its products until standard sanitary protocols are strictly met and verified by the regulator.
In a separate enforcement measure, the food safety authority has directed a prominent spice manufacturing firm to execute an immediate nationwide recall of its "Pre-packed Cumin Powder".
The recall directive was issued after official laboratory analysis declared samples of the packaged product "UNSAFE" for human consumption under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The FBO was further directed to undertake corrective measures to prevent recurrence of the incident and submit a report upon completion of the recall.
Earlier on Saturday, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said a sample of low-fat dairy whitener manufactured by a food brand and collected from the premises of a hotel chain in Connaught Place, New Delhi, has been declared "substandard" and "unsafe" in a Food Analyst's laboratory report under the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.
According to the findings, the sample was drawn from the premises of the hotel chain in Connaught Place in the national capital. The Food Analyst's laboratory report found the sample to be "substandard" and "unsafe", indicating non-compliance with the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006.
A copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the Food Business Operator (FBO) for reference and necessary action.
Following the findings, a notice was issued to the hotel chain regarding the non-compliant product.
